newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila wheat buying seen ebbing, unless prices dip.
newsitem.headline: Manila wheat buying seen ebbing, unless prices dip.

text.p: After a spate of orders in the past several weeks, Philippine grains and oilseeds importers are expected to stay out of the market in the coming week unless lured by softer prices, traders said.
On Thursday, Philippine mills bought 65,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat for May shipment.
Traders said most Philippine firms were fully covered on their wheat, soybean and soymeal requirement up to June.
"If prices fall to better levels then we can place orders for our July or August requirements" said an executive in a Philippine flour mill.
Philippine traders said they expected U.S. wheat prices to slide next week on talk the extent of damage of the U.S. wheat crop due to bad weather was lower than expected.
No fresh rice orders from the state-owned National Food Authority were expected, traders said.
"But everybody's waiting for the schedule on the country's plan to import some 350,000 tonnes of corn this year," said another trader.
The NFA has so far imported 120,000 tonnes of yellow corn from China and 25,000 tonnes of U.S. white corn since the start of the year.
The average retail price of yellow corn dipped to 9.81 pesos ($0.37) per kilogram from last week's 9.82. White corn fell to 9.83 pesos from 9.84.
The retail price of hard flour remained steady at 290 pesos per 25-kg bag. The price of white flour was also unchanged for the week at 260 pesos. Conversion $1 = 26.30 pesos
